title: HealthLink hybrid on-prem + hosted routing proposal
summary: Draft proposal for HealthLink POC: deploy a hybrid inference topology that keeps PHI processing on customer-managed on-prem GPUs while leveraging Redwood hosted inference for non-PHI and burst capacity. Focus is on clear routing policy, safe KV/prefix caching across trust boundaries, measurable latency SLOs, and an incremental canary rollout path.
customer_context: HealthLink is a regional healthcare provider with strict PHI residency rules. They want an LLM assistant to summarize visit notes and surface clinical suggestions. Non-PHI tasks (public content summarization, template generation) can run in hosted. They require audit logs, KMS integration, and the ability to run heavy models on-site for sensitive inputs. They prefer a minimal network surface between their VPC and Redwood.
constraints_and_requirements:
- PHI must never leave customer-controlled network in unencrypted form.
- Support for mutual TLS and ephemeral token exchange between Redwood control plane and on-prem agents.
- Ability to route requests by data classification tag and by account-tier.
- Latency targets: p50 <= 120ms for single-turn note summarization on on-prem; p95 <= 500ms for hosted non-PHI during 95th percentile traffic.
- Canaryable rollouts with automatic rollback on quality regressions.
- Operator visibility: per-request tracing, per-model cost breakdown, and audit logs stored in HealthLink's Splunk/ELK.
- Minimal on-prem footprint: single NVIDIA A10x2 node for baseline POC, scale-to-three for load testing.
architecture_options:
Option A: Full Private (on-prem-only) — All inference and model artifacts stored on-prem. Pros: max data control. Cons: higher ops burden for HealthLink and longer spin-up.

Option B: Split-routing (recommended POC) — Sensitive inputs routed to on-premized Redwood Private agent; non-sensitive routed to Redwood hosted API. Shared control plane for routing and observability. Pros: lower cost, fast time-to-value for non-sensitive flows. Cons: cross-boundary coordination and caching complexity.

Option C: Dedicated-hosted-only — Reserve Dedicated capacity in Redwood cloud, bring necessary compliance controls to meet HealthLink audit needs. Pros: simpler for Redwood to manage; Cons: may not meet strict PHI residency for certain customers.
recommended_solution:
Start with Option B: Split-routing POC. Deploy a lightweight Private Agent (containerized) inside HealthLink VPC that runs a quantized Llama-variant for PHI flows. The Redwood control plane will host a curated small family of models for public flows. Implement routing by a classification pre-step: the incoming payload is tokenized and a small deterministic classifier tags data as PHI/non-PHI before sending tokenized context to appropriate venue. Ensure message-level encryption with customer KMS for any token exchange.

Key design notes: 1) No raw PHI stored in Redwood hosted logs. 2) On-prem KV cache used for repeated patient contexts; only cache keys that are deterministic hashes salted with a per-tenant secret. 3) Use model pinning so HealthLink can freeze model versions on-prem for regulatory validation.
routing_policy_spec:
- Classifier at edge (agent) with model id hc-classifier-v1. Runs in ~6ms.
- Policy table: (tag:PHI) -> on-prem agent; (tag:NON_PHI) -> hosted-llm-default.
- Fallback: if on-prem agent unavailable, route to hosted-fallback only if HealthLink toggles "allow-remote-fallback" for the test cohort; otherwise return 503.
- Rate limiting: per-tenant token budget enforced at the control plane. Bursting allowed from Dedicated pool if explicit burst-capacity flag is set.
- Authentication: mutual TLS + short-lived signed JWT issued by HealthLink's IdP using OIDC.
- Observability: X-Request-ID propagated; trace includes routing decision, model id, response latencies, and cache hit/miss tag.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (sanity): dev loop with synthetic PHI data in lab on 1 A10 node. Verify model pinning, KMS integration, and auditing.
Phase 1 (shadow): 10% of production traffic duplicated to on-prem (no live responses) for metric comparators. Monitor latency, token costs, and failure modes for 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (canary): 5% live routing to on-prem for internal users; rollback on any of: p95 latency increase >30%, model quality delta >2% on evaluation prompts, or any PHI leakage in logs.
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): 25% -> 50% -> 100% over days/weeks with automated checks and human gate at each step.
Phase 4 (stress test): scale to 3 nodes, run peak-hour replay and verify autoscaling and cost delta metrics.
measurement_and_slo:
- Latency: p50 <= 120ms on-prem; p95 <= 500ms hosted non-PHI.
- Availability: on-prem agent 99.5% during business hours for POC; hosted endpoints 99.95%.
- Cost: compare per-token unit cost on hosted vs estimated on-prem fully loaded cost; track run-rate deviation weekly.
- Quality: monitor eval set of 200 prompts for hallucination/regression; maintain mean F1 >= baseline and track ROUGE/semantic-similarity deltas.
- Security: zero incidents of PHI exfiltration; daily integrity checks for audit logs.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Classifier mislabeling PHI as non-PHI -> mitigation: conservative classifier thresholds, fail-closed default to on-prem for ambiguous cases.
Risk: KV cache exposes deterministic patient identifiers -> mitigation: salt hashes with tenant secret rotated monthly; only store hashed keys, strip raw identifiers before caching.
Risk: Network partition prevents on-prem access -> mitigation: explicit policy to either fail-safe (reject) or route to hosted fallback only for signed test cohorts; instrument alerts.
Risk: Model quality drift when using quantized on-prem models -> mitigation: nightly eval harness and automatic rollback if regressions exceed threshold.
Risk: Operational complexity for HealthLink -> mitigation: provide managed runbook, 2-week on-call overlap from Redwood SRE for POC, and a concierge onboarding checklist.
open_questions:
- Does HealthLink require HSM-backed key wraps for every inference request or only for model artifact encryption at rest?
- Which internal teams own the decision to allow hosted-fallback during outages? Legal/Security/Product?
- Will HealthLink accept a short-term sandbox where non-PHI labeling is manually spot-checked during Phase 1?
- Are there regulatory audit formats (schema) that HealthLink requires for logs beyond standard JSON lines?
- Can HealthLink commit to maintaining an internal classifier model or prefer Redwood-managed classifier as part of the POC?
